definition: Interpolating an external language model's scores into ASR beam search at decode time, biasing recognition toward in-domain vocabulary without retraining the acoustic model.
details: Interpolating an external language model's scores into ASR beam search at decode time, biasing recognition toward in-domain vocabulary without retraining the acoustic model. The cheapest form of ASR domain adaptation, with deep and cold fusion as the trained alternatives.

explainer.lead: Shallow fusion blends an external language model's scores into ASR beam search at decode time, biasing recognition toward in-domain vocabulary without retraining the acoustic model. It is the cheapest form of ASR domain adaptation.

tiers.eli5: While transcribing speech, the system lets a second model that knows your special vocabulary nudge the choice of words, without retraining the main listener.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add a weighted term to the beam search score to favour in-domain words, leaving the acoustic model untouched. A pitfall is that a too-large weight over-biases output and increases errors, so the weight must be tuned.
tiers.paperLevel: At each beam step the combined score is the acoustic model log-probability plus a weight times the external language model log-probability; deep and cold fusion are the trained alternatives. Limits include needing a good in-domain language model and sensitivity to the weight.

explainer.example: A medical dictation system adds a language model of clinical terms so drug names are recognised without fine-tuning the acoustic model.
